turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's birefringence at 1064 nm, then select the 5 candidates whose
birefringence is CLOSEST to 0.1.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
Cubic crystals (identical lattice vectors, 90° angles) are optically isotropic, so \(\Delta n=0\). Extreme vdW-layered or 1-D chain packings produce \(\Delta n\gtrsim0.2\). Wurtzite/chalcopyrite-derived packings (c/a near the ideal zinc-blende values) give only \(\Delta n\approx0.03{-}0.06\). The five structures whose lattice anisotropy, bonding dimensionality and polarizable-anion alignment lie between these limits are therefore predicted to have \(\Delta n(1064\,\text{nm})\) nearest 0.1:

- c054 (tetragonal CsLi\(_2\)I\(_3\), c/a = 2.36, mixed ionic/covalent layers),
- c046 (tetragonal KLiZnS\(_2\), ionic ZnS layers separated by K),
- c067 (isostructural Rb analogue),
- c006 (pseudo-cubic but polarizable GaSe\(_4\)/Cl framework),
- c085 (hexagonal perovskite-like RbSnCl\(_3\), face-sharing octahedral chains).

Final: c054, c046, c067, c006, c085
